messages:
Priya S: Heads-up — Sentinel (enterprise) opened a sizing convo for Q4. They want a firm commit for Black Friday + 2-week holiday window. Current baseline usage we've measured is ~360k GPU-hours/mo. They asked what buffer policy we recommend and how to price burst/failover. Any quick back-of-envelope numbers?
Alex R: rough math first pass: baseline 360k GPU-hrs/mo -> that's ~12k GPU-hrs/day. If BF weekend + seasonal spike ~1.8x daily peak -> peak ~21.6k GPU-hrs/day. For a 2-week window assume average 1.4x -> ~16.8k/day.
Alex R: propose reserved commit = baseline * 1.1 (10% cushion) + burst pool for holiday ~= baseline * 0.7 for 2 weeks. So: commit ~396k/mo, holiday burst pool (monthly-equivalent spread) add ~252k/ month for 2 weeks of heavy use.
Alex R: quick code block math: ```
# baseline
baseline_month = 360000  # GPU-hours
commit = baseline_month * 1.10  # 10% cushion
holiday_burst_equiv = (baseline_month * (1.4 - 1.0) * 14/30)  # extra for 2-week window
commit, holiday_burst_equiv
# ~396000, ~168000
```
Matt L: couple network/ops caveats: Sentinel's primary region is eu-west. Our eu-west warm pool is limited — current hot nodes for dedicated are ~120 GPUs free for reassign. Cross-region failover to us-west is possible but adds egress + latency. Cold-start times for new nodes in eu-west are around 9-12 mins with current image; warmup with cached KV takes ~2-3 mins. So burst sizing has to include prewarmed capacity or they'll see latency spikes.
Matt L: recommendation: reserve extra 48-72h prewarmed headroom for holiday start. That reduces cold-start risk. Also check NIC quotas with infra team — some customers hit soft limits last year.
Evan C: cost perspective — if our committed price is $1.40/GPU-hr and burst on-demand is $2.45/GPU-hr, the delta is material. For the commit numbers Alex suggested (396k committed + 168k equivalent burst) effective monthly cost: commit_cost ~ $554k, burst_equiv_cost delta if used = (2.45-1.40)*168k ~= $176k extra for that month.
Evan C: quick line: if they pay for a larger commit to cover holiday (i.e., bump commit -> 560k), they save on per-hour cost but increase committed spend baseline. We should show 3 options: conservative (10% buffer + burst), heavy-commit (cover 90% of peak), and hybrid (commit + limited burst pool).
Priya S: can you sketch those 3 options in a tiny table? I'll include in proposal to AE. Need to call out cross-region fallback cost and latency impact. Also need SLA change for warm pool guarantee.
Alex R: tiny table pasted: ```
Option A: conservative
 - Commit: 396k GPU-hrs/mo
 - Burst pool: up to 250k (2-week window)
 - Ops: prewarm 48h at holiday start
Option B: heavy-commit
 - Commit: 560k GPU-hrs/mo (covers ~90% peak)
 - Burst pool: minimal (50k)
 - Ops: standard warmup
Option C: hybrid
 - Commit: 460k GPU-hrs/mo
 - Burst pool: 150k
 - Ops: prewarm 24-48h, cross-region fallback enabled
```
Nadia (oncall-bot): eu-west cluster status: capacity_headroom=120 GPUs, pending_image_builds=2, avg_cold_start=10m. Tagging @eng-infra for NIC quota check.
deploy-bot: Reminder: schedule maintenance windows for prewarm builds. See https://infra.ops/schedule (automated message).
Matt L: one more note — network egress to us-west add ~80-120ms RTT; for their latency SLO (<= 120ms gen response) that could push them over. If we do cross-region fallback, we need to route only non-latency-critical routes or reduce token parallelism.
Priya S: ok this is actionable. Evan/Alex — can you convert to a 1-pager with the three numbered options + direct $ delta and a recommended default (my vote: Option C with 20% committed buffer + 48h prewarm + 150k burst pool). I'll send to AE and calendar a 15-min handoff with Sentinel.
Evan C: will draft 1-pager and show commit vs break-even point.
Alex R: I'll run a simulation for expected GPU-hours distribution over the 2-week window and share CSV.
Priya S: thanks. tagging @support to prep runbook for holiday oncall. :thumbsup:
Support: got it, will standby and create runbook checklist.
